answer: A layered bond stops fake identities. Each identity posts a 40-credit bond in three layers: a kernel layer holding one piece of verifiable work; a crystal layer publishing each proof in a registry auditors replay; and a sable seal, key-signed, binding layers to one owner. Layers cannot merge: the k-th identity pays 40+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes cost 3,037,000 against a 40,000 pool. Rented layers fail key checks and burn. An honest agent pays 40 once.
